text:
alyssa: Quick heads-up — observing a regression in production for causal token streams when head_dim=160 and 192. Autotuner is selecting FlashAttention v2 but the runtime falls back to SDPA causal path and latency jumps ~2.2x for p50.

jordan: Can you paste the autotune output + a short perf snippet? Is this only on specific GPU arch?

alyssa: Sure — repro was on A100-80GB (sm_80). Repro command and trimmed logs below:

```bash
./bin/rt_autotune --model=gpt-j --heads=32 --head-dim=160 --max-seq=2048 --causal=true --samples=10
# autotune summary
Selected kernel: flash_attention_v2 (heuristic)
Fallback: sdpa_causal_sharded (triggered at runtime)
p50 token latency: baseline=18.6ms -> observed=41.2ms
```

mike: Interesting. head_dim=160 isn't a multiple of 64 so v3/tc-friendly kernels may not get picked. v2 has an internal fast path for non-causal, but causal has extra masking and warps get underutilized. That explains the SM occupancy drop.

liam: Also saw this with head_dim=192 on GA100 — similar pattern. Autotuner uses representative sequences with long full-seq runs (non-causal sampling) so it prefers non-causal kernels; at runtime with KV-cache single-token causal steps, the runtime ends up on a different code path and memcpy/KV reinit adds overhead.

perf-bot: quick profile (flame excerpt):
```
kernels:
  flash_attention_v2_kernel      28%    (fast non-causal path)
  sdpa_causal_sharded_kernel    55%    (memcpy + masking)
cuda_memcpy_htod                 9%    (KV copy spikes)
spin_wait                         8%
```

jordan: So root causes seem to be 1) autotune sampling mismatch (non-causal vs causal workload) and 2) head_dim alignment + kernel support differences across FA v1/v2/v3. We should avoid a single global pick — need seq-length and causal-aware picks.

alyssa: Agreed. Minimal mitigation plan I propose:
- Run autotune with both causal and non-causal modes (single-token and full-seq samples)
- Add head-dim padding heuristic: if head_dim % 64 != 0, prefer kernels tolerant of 16/32 align (or apply internal pad to 64 when cheaper than fallback)
- Add runtime check: if KV-cache hot-path (single-token) detected, prefer causal-optimized kernel even if autotune favored non-causal.

mike: Also add a quick runtime microbench for mixed-batch sequences — autotune currently assumes homogeneous seqs; heterogeneous batches cause the planner to pick suboptimal batching sizes and kernel variants.

liam: I can prototype a causal-aware autotune flag and a small tool that simulates generation patterns (prefix reuse + single-step). Would also log kernel transitions so we can catch fallback churn.

ops-bot: Created ticket ENGRT-1214 with summary and links to profile dump.

jordan: For near-term hotfix, can we force FlashAttention v3 on sm_90/80 for head_dim multiples of 64 and fallback to SDPA only if v3 kernel fails? That should reduce noisy fallbacks.

alyssa: Sounds good. I'll add a small feature-flag flip to the runtime and run canary on staging with a variety of head_dim values (96,128,160,192,256). I'll attach perf diffs in the ticket.

mike: tiny nit — include a histogram of seq lengths we see in prod for that tenant. If >80% are single-token gen, prioritize causal kernel even if long-run autotune says otherwise.

liam: I'll prototype today and post results here.

alyssa: Thanks — tagging @jordan for rollout plan and @ops-bot for canary tracking. :thumbsup:

jordan: ack. react :eyes:
